title: Geometric sections of a finite Weil scheme and the local return operators
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0=\mathbf F_q,k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $Z_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], put $Z=Z_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal G$ be a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $Z_0$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-weil-constructible-heart]. Write $V=H_c^0(Z,\mathcal G)$ for geometric compactly supported cohomology [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], with its geometric Frobenius $F$ [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], interpreted at a common finite coefficient-field stage as in the Weil-sheaf definition. For a closed point $x\in|Z_0|$, put $d_x=[\kappa(x):k_0]$ and let $P_x$ be the set of $k$-morphisms $z:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Z$ whose projection to $Z_0$ has image $x$. Let $\mathcal G_z$ denote the geometric stalk at $z$, and let $F_{x,z}$ be its degree-$d_x$ local geometric-Frobenius operator [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], also extended from a common finite coefficient-field stage.

The set $|Z_0|$ is finite, $|P_x|=d_x\geq1$, and evaluation on geometric stalks gives a $\Qlb$-linear isomorphism
$$e:V\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{x\in|Z_0|}\ \bigoplus_{z\in P_x}\mathcal G_z.$$
The vector space $V$ is finite-dimensional and $F$ is an automorphism. Under $e$, $F$ preserves each summand $V_x=\bigoplus_{z\in P_x}\mathcal G_z$ and permutes its stalk summands cyclically, by linear isomorphisms. If $e_z:V\to\mathcal G_z$ is the component of $e$, then
$$e_z\circ F^{d_x}=F_{x,z}\circ e_z\qquad(z\in P_x).$$
The evaluation isomorphism is natural for morphisms of constructible Weil sheaves. No reducedness of $Z_0$ and no weight or semisimplicity hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), the geometric base change $a_Z$ is finite. The finite structure morphism is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Use its identity compactification; [lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius] gives the natural identification $R\Gamma_c(Z,M)\simeq R\Gamma(Z,M)$, including the specified transports. Apply [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image] to $a_Z:Z\to s$ and its geometric point $\operatorname{id}_s$. Its finite indexing set $P_{\operatorname{id}_s}$ is $Z(k)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(s,Z)$, and its restriction-map formula gives $e:H_c^0(Z,\mathcal G)\simeq\bigoplus_{z\in Z(k)}\mathcal G_z$. Its naturality is for all morphisms of the underlying constructible sheaves, so also for morphisms of Weil sheaves. No assertion about $|Z_0|$ or dimensions is used yet.

proof.text: For a closed point $x$ of $Z_0$, finite type follows from finiteness of its structure morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a) gives a finite residue extension of positive degree $d_x$. By [def-weil-geometric-point], its lifts are the $k_0$-embeddings $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k$. The finite-field Galois theorem [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius] says this extension is separable and Galois, with its $d_x$ automorphisms the powers of $c\mapsto c^q$; after one embedding, all embeddings are obtained by those powers. Hence $|P_x|=d_x\geq1$. The projection from the finite set $Z(k)$ of step 1 onto $|Z_0|$ is surjective, so $|Z_0|$ is finite. Write $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, $g=g_Z$, and $T(z)=gz h^{-1}$ using [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. This source reparametrization makes $T(z)$ a $k$-point. On residue-field embeddings it is composition with $\gamma^{-1}$, so $T$ acts on each $P_x$ in a cycle of length $d_x$; in particular $g^{d_x}z=z h^{d_x}$.

proof.text: Regroup the finite sum of step 1 by the fibres $P_x$. For the underlying degree-zero complex $M=\operatorname{For}\mathcal G$, [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] interprets $\mathcal G_z$ as $\mathrm H^0(\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*M))$ at a common finite coefficient-field stage and states that this is finite-dimensional. A finite direct sum of these spaces is finite-dimensional, so $V$ is finite-dimensional. Scalar extension from that stage to $\Qlb$ preserves this assertion.

proof.text:
Work at a common field stage $E$, and put $C=R\Gamma_c(Z,-)$, $P=Lg^*$, $P_r=L(g^r)^*$. By [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], $F=C(\theta)\tau_{c,M}$. The transports are natural in every underlying derived morphism by [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Before replacing $P^r$ by $P_r$, induction gives
$$F^r=C(\theta\circ P\theta\circ\cdots\circ P^{r-1}\theta)\circ\tau_{c,P^{r-1}M}\circ\cdots\circ\tau_{c,M}.$$
The base $r=1$ is the definition. For the induction step, expand $F\circ F^r$ and move $\tau_{c,M}$ past the morphism $C(\theta\circ\cdots\circ P^{r-1}\theta)$ by naturality; the new sheaf-map factor is $\theta\circ P(\theta\circ\cdots\circ P^{r-1}\theta)$. Under the associative comparison of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], rationalized as in the local-operator definition, this is $\theta^{[r+1]}$ of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Thus
$$F^r=C(\theta^{[r]})\circ\tau^{[r]}_{c,M},$$
where $\tau^{[r]}$ is the iterated transport of [lem-a1-proper-sections-semilinear-germs]. This induction uses no assertion about reduction of a rational Weil isomorphism to an invertible lattice map.

source.place: First sentence and displayed evaluation formula, corrected geometric-stalk interpretation

proof.text:
Let $z_r=T^rz$. Apply [lem-a1-proper-sections-semilinear-germs] to $Z_0,M,r,z$. The naturality of the derived germs, defined by the counit in that lemma, applied to $\theta^{[r]}:P_rM\to M$, and the identity of step 4 give
$$e_zF^r=\mathrm H^0\!\left(\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*\theta^{[r]})\circ\operatorname{Fib}_s(b_{r,z,M})\circ I_{Lz_r^*M}^{[r]}\right)e_{z_r}.$$
Here $b_{r,z,M}$ uses $g^rz=z_rh^r$; the lemma explicitly identifies evaluation after the specified compact-support exchange and point transport with this composite. For $r=1$ all three maps in parentheses are isomorphisms: the Weil structure is an isomorphism, $b_{1,z,M}$ is a pullback-composition comparison, and point transport is invertible by [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso](1). Thus the only nonzero block in output stalk $z$ is the isomorphism from input stalk $Tz$. Consequently $F$ preserves each $V_x$ and permutes its stalk summands in the cycle $T^{-1}$. All formulas extend from the common stage to $\Qlb$.

proof.text:
Fix $x$ and $z\in P_x$, and take $r=d_x$ in step 5. Step 2 gives $z_r=z$ and the equality of scheme maps $g^rz=zh^r$. Consequently the coefficient of $e_z$ in that formula is
$$\mathrm H^0\!\left(\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*\theta^{[r]})\circ\operatorname{Fib}_s(b_{r,z,M})\circ I_{Lz^*M}^{[r]}\right).$$
The three arrows, in this order, are the final stalk map, middle composition comparison, and initial iterated point transport in the displayed definition of $F_{x,z}$ in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. They use the same specified pullback-composition comparisons; in particular the return is $g^rz=zh^r$, not $g^rz=z$. The coefficient therefore is $F_{x,z}$ by that definition, proving $e_zF^{d_x}=F_{x,z}e_z$.

proof.text: A permutation of a finite collection of summands, with an isomorphism on every block, is invertible: use the inverse permutation and the inverse stalk maps. Conjugating by $e$ proves that $F$ is an automorphism of $V$. The naturality of $e$ was obtained in step 1. For empty $Z_0$ both sides are zero and this is the unique automorphism of the zero space.

The item states the correct sum of geometric stalks, so nothing is weakened. New node: the identity is type-correct, and T(z)=g z h^{-1} is a k-point because a_Y g = h a_Y. It is the derived form of transport of structure: the germ of g^*s at z is h^*(z_1^* s), and h^* on sections is the point transport. It holds on the cases I tried (Spec k_0, empty scheme, M=0, Spec F_{q^2}). It is not a restatement of the parent: it has no Weil structure and allows any proper Y_0. It is not a duplicate of lem-trf-graph-frobenius-point-exchange, lem-trf-finite-scheme-derived-germs, lem-trf-compact-frobenius-transport-composition, lem-pod-frobenius-exchange-degree-zero or lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image, which are finite-coefficient, k-endomorphism-only or have no germs. Item steps: step 2 correctly gives the projection of T(z) as gamma^{-1} i, a d_x-cycle, and the return g^d z = z h^d. Step 4's induction F^r = C(theta^[r]) tau^[r] checks against theta^[n+1] = theta^[n] L(g^n)^* theta via the associativity of lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition. Step 5 gives blocks permuted by T^{-1}, invertible by lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso (1). Step 6 matches the displayed definition in def-weil-local-frobenius-trace arrow by arrow.
